reference.title: OIDC configuration fields
reference.shortdesc: Configure OpenID Connect client credentials, endpoints, and token behavior for Red Hat Quay login.

section.p: You can configure Red Hat Quay to authenticate users through any OpenID Connect (OIDC)-compatible identity provider, including Azure Entra ID (formerly Azure AD), Okta, Keycloak, and others. These fields define the necessary client credentials, endpoints, and token behavior used during the OIDC login flow.

entry.p: The parent key that holds the OIDC configuration settings. Typically the name of the OIDC provider, for example, AZURE_LOGIN_CONFIG, however any arbitrary string is accepted.
The registered client ID for this Red Hat Quay instance. Example:0e8dbe15c4c7630b6780
The registered client secret for this Red Hat Quay instance. Example:e4a58ddd3d7408b7aec109e85564a0d153d3e846

Used when the internal authorization is set to LDAP. Red Hat Quay reads this parameter and tries to search through the LDAP tree for the user with this username. If it exists, it automatically creates a link to that LDAP account.
Scopes Red Hat Quay requests during the OIDC login flow. Must include openid. Each scope listed here must also appear in the IdP’s scopes_supported array from /.well-known/openid-configuration.
Support for custom query parameters on OIDC endpoints. The following endpoints are supported: authorization_endpoint, token_endpoint, and user_endpoint.

Allows the user to define the issuer to verify. For example, JWT tokens container a parameter known as iss which defines who issued the token. By default, this is read from the .well-know/openid/configuration endpoint, which is exposed by every OIDC provider. If this verification fails, there is no login.

Accepted issuer URLs for this provider. When set, Red Hat Quay accepts tokens whose iss claim matches any entry. Use this field to accept multiple issuers, for example Microsoft Entra ID v1.0 and v2.0 URLs during migration. If not set, Red Hat Quay uses OIDC_ISSUER.

Accepted audience values for bearer token and On-Behalf-Of (OBO) flows. When set, Red Hat Quay validates the token aud claim against this list. CLIENT_ID is always implicitly included. If not set, audience validation defaults to CLIENT_ID.

Optional whitelist of authorized party (azp) client IDs. When set, only tokens from these client applications are accepted. If not set, all clients are accepted. When restricting OBO clients, include your application’s own CLIENT_ID so direct user login continues to work.
The OIDC discovery base URL for authentication. Red Hat Quay uses path joining for OIDC discovery, so the URL must end with a trailing /. Example:https://login.microsoftonline.com/<tenant-id>/v2.0/
Sets the preferred username to a parameter from the token.
Changes the icon on the login screen.
The name of the service that is being authenticated. Example:Microsoft Entra ID
The name of the claim that is used to verify the email address of the user.
The key name within the OIDC token payload that holds information about the user’s group memberships.

Whether to allow or disable the /userinfo endpoint. If using Azure Entra ID, this field must be set to True because Azure obtains the user’s information from the token instead of calling the /userinfo endpoint.
Whether to enable support for Proof Key for Code Exchange.
The code challenge method used to generate the code_challenge sent in the initial authorization request.
Whether to omit client_secret during token request when the client is public.
